name: Projection

subjectOf.text: Capturing only 5 to 10 percent of yield-driven capital flows through voucher reward merchant ecosystems would make LER a significant player in the market.
subjectOf.abstract: If LER can only capture 5-10% of these yield-driven flows through voucher reward merchant ecosystems, LER become a significant player in this evolving market segment.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5454054
scope_conditions: assuming a TAM above $1 trillion from reallocating capital

subjectOf.text: Activists currently prevail in about forty percent of proxy contests, and by rallying passive retail and institutional voters LER could cut that success rate by fifteen to thirty percentage points.
subjectOf.abstract: Extrapolating from earlier studies on activist success rates, LER could reduce activist success rates by 15–30% just by rallying retail and institutional support, thus creating a resilient ownership base that prioritizes the company's long-term vision
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Liquid Equity Rewards in Corporate America (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5583610
scope_conditions: extrapolated from shareholder perk and loyalty studies rather than observed LER deployments

description: 2 claims in the published works of Wulf A. Kaal carry the concept tag 'projection'. Derived node: a roster, not an adjudicated definition.
